spans.text: The road as a window manager — Tier 1

Status: `spec`; standalone Linux Tier 1 and two-app handoff proofs implemented. An initial road surface is integrated into Super in a separate window; the full road-shell product is not implemented. Six decisions remain open in §13.
The scope ruling in §1 is Travis's, 2026-09-10. Everything downstream of it is a proposal.

Five things were tightened and each is recorded as a correction in DOCTRINE rather than edited away: the live budget is separate from pose eligibility (§4.1); a sign says three things, not one (§5.1); the capability layer is only half the authority boundary (§6.1); the liveness wording was too absolute (§10.1); and "macOS is easier" is a hypothesis with a test list (§11). §12 is now the single narrow proof to build before anything accumulates around it.
A road that manages web apps needs no new operating system, and no new primitive.
The Tauri host, the multi-webview primitive, the per-pane authority boundary, the slot allocator, the op seam, and the three-tier residency ladder all exist and are measured. What does not exist is a
— and the manifest that says which app may stand where.

Moving a pane to another dash must not cancel, pause or reroute its work — and dispatching work to an app must not move its pane. The single most likely way to ruin this design is to let one gesture do both.
